decisions.reason: The accepted stainless-steel whisk is already captured by the candidate's message 64 MODIFY, including removal of the superseded whisk-style reference; the motor-speed cap belongs to the separate variable-speed requirement.
The whisk selection and 1500 RPM motor cap do not change the established 2.5-quart bowl capacity, depth, or enclosure geometry.
The source decision concerns the whisk and motor speed, not the spout's material, geometry, orientation, or appearance.
Setting a maximum motor speed does not alter the existing splash target or conditional splash-guard policy.
The component selections do not change the requirement to deliver the initial system layout in CAD.
The source constrains motor and controller selection but does not change the independently requested basic wiring-plan deliverable.
Neither the selected whisk nor the maximum motor speed changes the solenoid-based dispensing sequence, flow behavior, or gravity-feed requirement.
The candidate already has a message 64 MODIFY that completely records the client-set maximum motor speed of 1500 RPM.
The new speed cap does not modify the standing requirement that the unit remain stable without rattling or shifting.
The source narrows specific whisk and motor-control selections but does not change the prototype-wide strategy of using off-the-shelf electronic components.
The whisk and motor-speed choices do not affect the requirement that bowls be quickly removable and swappable.
The source decision has no effect on the device's beige body or green accents.
